title: The Governance Scope's mandate is protecting a resilient equilibrium, not administering governance well
content:
A.1 states that the Governance Scope regulates the governance processes and balance of power of the Sky Ecosystem, and that it "must ensure that the resilient equilibrium of Sky Governance remains protected against all potential direct and indirect threats."

Two choices of wording carry the weight. First, the object of protection is an **equilibrium**, not a process or an outcome — governance is modelled as a dynamic system that can be knocked out of balance, so the Scope's job is stability rather than throughput. Second, the threat surface is explicitly extended to **indirect** threats, which licenses intervention against things that are not attacks on governance but merely create conditions for one (concentration of delegate power, dependency on a single facilitator, erosion of documentation quality).

The practical consequence is a bias toward caution and toward pre-emptive structural rules. A Scope charged only with running governance would evaluate proposals on their merits; a Scope charged with protecting equilibrium against indirect threats must also ask what precedent or power concentration a proposal creates. Much of the rest of A.1 — err-on-the-side-of-caution duties, precedent requirements, layered immutability — is downstream of this framing.
description: A.1 frames the Scope defensively: it must protect Sky Governance's equilibrium against all potential direct AND indirect threats, making threat-modelling the default posture.
